q: When heat is transferred from one object to another object the total heat lost by one object is equal to the total heat gained by the other object.
e: True. When heat is transferred from one object to another object the total heat lost by one object is equal to the total heat gained by the other object. Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule.

q: According to the law of heat exchange, $\Delta Q_{lost} = \Delta Q_{gained}$.
e: True. According to the law of heat exchange, ΔQlost = ΔQgained. Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule.

q: Since heat is a form of energy, the law of heat exchange is one particular statement of the law of conservation of energy.
e: True. Since heat is a form of energy, the law of heat exchange is one particular statement of the law of conservation of energy. If only conservative forces act, kinetic plus potential stays constant.

q: The specific heat capacity of a substance can be determined using the law of heat exchange.
e: True. The specific heat capacity of a substance can be determined using the law of heat exchange. Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ.

q: A calorimeter is a device used to measure the heat flow of a chemical reaction or physical change.
e: True. A calorimeter is a device used to measure the heat flow of a chemical reaction or physical change. A calorimeter measures heat by the temperature change of a known mass of water.

q: A calorimeter mainly consists of a metallic vessel made of copper (or) aluminium.
e: True. A calorimeter mainly consists of a metallic vessel made of copper (or) aluminium. A calorimeter measures heat by the temperature change of a known mass of water.

q: The metallic vessel with a stirrer for stirring the contents in the vessel is kept in an insulating jacket to prevent heat lost to the environment.
e: True. The metallic vessel with a stirrer for stirring the contents in the vessel is kept in an insulating jacket to prevent heat lost to the environment. Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule.

q: Total heat gained by the sample and calorimeter is $\Delta Q_{gained} = mc\Delta T + m_c c_c \Delta T$.
e: True. Total heat gained by the sample and calorimeter is ΔQgained = mcΔT + m_c c_c ΔT. A calorimeter measures heat by the temperature change of a known mass of water.

q: By the law of heat exchange, $\Delta Q_{gained} = \Delta Q_{lost}$.
e: True. By the law of heat exchange, ΔQgained = ΔQlost. Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule.
